chapter: Garland: early Ory band and bass craft
title: Old bassist Albert Glenny and three- and four-string basses
summary: The interviewer asks about Albert Glenny, the oldest bass player, and they compare his basses and four-string bass use.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Uh... I was gonna ask a little bit more about any other bass players. Do you remember old man Glenny Albert?
Albert Glenny? Yeah, I remember Glenny.
That was one of the old timers. He just died this year, you know.
He was 88 years old when he died. What? 88, uh-huh.
He was considered about the oldest musician there. He sold his bass about 2 years ago, but until he was about 86, he still had his bass.
Hmm. Well, he was older than, uh... Uh... Uh... What do you mean? What am I trying to call? Slowdrag? Oh, Slowdrag. Oh, yeah.
He's a lot older than Slowdrag. Oh, yeah. Yeah, I know that old man. Slowdrag's just about, oh, something like 70 this year, I think. I'll be doggone.
The Glenny was 18 years older, yeah.
Whew. Well, there I remember, I can remember him good.
He had a full-size bass. He had a big bass. When I was a kid, I can remember that. I remember him good.
I think they say he used a three-string bass for years, but when I first met him, he was using four-string.

Well, later years, they all used a four-string bass. Yeah, they all used. They all used a four-string bass. I've got quite a few of them. I don't know who it could be, and I wouldn't know how to... Very few... Half, they know nothing at all. Can't sing a E-string now, make those pedal notes.
Yeah, well, they never used those much, I guess.
